info.title: Sortyard API
info.summary: The one door the operator console, agents (MCP) and the conductor all use.
info.description: Sortyard API, Phase 0 (design draft §4, §7). Resource shapes are the frozen §3 JSON Schemas beside this file, referenced, never re-declared. Every operation names the roles that may invoke it in `x-sortyard-roles` and as alternative `security` requirements; agent-invocable operations are exposed as MCP tools named by `x-sortyard-mcp-tool`. The permission matrix is summarised in PERMISSIONS.md; open questions are recorded in NOTES.md. Every mutation writes an AuditLog entry and ledger Events.

post.description: Only for an `agent-service-account` RoleBinding. The permission set is the agent role's column of the matrix (PERMISSIONS.md). Issuance refuses (422) any token whose permissions would include both task creation and claiming — the queue-poisoning vector (§7).

agent_role.description: The §7 agent role the token carries.

project_id.description: Project a sensor or grooming token is confined to.

stage_run_id.description: Stage run a build-worker token is confined to.

get.summary: A project's items that are not done, in link order
get.description: The tracker view of the workflow kernel (HARNESS-V3 section 3.2): a read of the projection the item workflow writes. An item comes after every item it is blocked by; items no link orders keep their creation order. Each item carries its state, owner, limit, reason and age. A project with no items, or one that does not exist, has an empty queue.

milestone_id.description: A grouping and a preferred shipping order; it never orders the queue.

state.description: The state the item's workflow last recorded; null before its first transition.

owner.description: The service that owns the item in this state.

age_seconds.description: Seconds since the item entered its state (since it was created, for an item not started).

blocked_by.description: Items of this queue the item is linked as blocked by.

post.summary: Admit an item: check its spec, create it and start its workflow
post.description: The one way an item enters the workflow kernel (HARNESS-V3 section 3.5, step 4). The item is checked before anything is created: its spec states an outcome and names at least one acceptance test, its lane is known and declares its repository and every need, every blocked_by link resolves to an item of this workspace, and its risk tier is one the state table has limits for. An item that fails is refused with every reason (`reasons`) and nothing is created. Otherwise the item, its links and its spec are stored and its workflow is started; the scheduler dispatches it when everything it is blocked by is merged and its lane has a free slot. Admitting the same id again with the same content changes nothing and answers 200; with other content it is refused (409), since a spec is written once.

id.description: The item's id; its branch is sortyard/<id>.

project_id.description: The project whose queue lists the item.

title.description: The item's title; its pull request carries it.

risk_tier.description: low, medium or high: sets the limits the state table gives by risk tier. Default medium.

milestone_id.description: A grouping and a preferred shipping order; it never orders the queue.

lane.description: The lane the item runs on: the name of a lane capability file.

repository.description: The one repository the change goes to, as owner/name. The lane must declare it.

needs.description: What the item needs beyond its lane's defaults, as references into the lane capability file (secret:NAME, service:NAME, repository:owner/name).

blocked_by.description: Items of this workspace that must be merged before this one is dispatched.

spec.description: The item's spec. It states an `outcome` and lists `acceptance`: at least one test, each {test, name}. Anything else in it is handed to the worker as written.

200.description: The item was admitted before with the same content; nothing changed.

201.description: Admitted: the item is stored and its workflow started.

422.description: Refused: the body is malformed, or the item fails admission. For a failed admission `reasons` lists every failure as `rule: what`, and nothing was created.

503.description: The service runs without a workflow engine or lane capability files, or the engine did not answer. Nothing was created.

get.summary: One item's transitions, in ledger order
get.description: Every transition of the item's workflow as a ledger Event: the state left, the state entered, the owner, the limit and the typed reason. `facts.lifecycle.kind` is the harness.lifecycle.v1 kind of the transition, or null where that format has none.

post.summary: Ask an item's workflow for a change
post.description: Nothing writes an item's state but its workflow. This sends the workflow a request, as a signal; the workflow puts it to the decision service, and the request, the answer and its source appear on the item's timeline. Accepted means the engine has the signal, not that the answer was the one asked for: an answer the item's decision state does not have is not granted, and a request that arrives as the item finishes is not acted on. The request is written to the audit log.

answer.description: The decision asked for. It is granted only if it is one of the answers of the decision state of the item's state table.

reason.description: Why the change is asked for.

202.description: Accepted: the request was delivered to the item's workflow.

503.description: The service runs without a workflow engine, or the engine did not answer.

operatorSession.description: Human operators via the installation's OIDC provider (§3.1). The listed role is the operator's RoleBinding role: admin, operator or viewer (§3.9).

serviceAccountToken.description: Scoped service-account token issued per agent role (§7): conductor, build-worker, sensor or grooming-agent. The listed role is the token's agent role.

reason_code.description: Machine reason, e.g. an unbound code or a policy refusal.

NextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page; null on the last page.

DecisionCreate.description: Create input for a Decision (§3.3, §7). A Decision is created unresolved: `state` must be `open` and the resolution fields (`resolution`, `answered_by`, `answer_channel`, `resolved_at`) are refused, so no creator can record an answer. Only `answerDecision` (operator accounts) answers; only `applyDecisionDefault` (conductor, past `decide_by`) defaults.

token.description: Bearer token; returned once, never retrievable again.

ContextPacket.description: An assembled context packet (§3.7a): content-hashed, in recipe order.

queue.description: Every visible task in computed order — ineligible ones included (HARNESS-238).

next_claims.description: Simulation of the next claims, in order.

Unauthorized.description: No valid operator session or service-account token.

Forbidden.description: The caller's role is not in this operation's x-sortyard-roles, or the token's scope (project / stage run) does not cover the target.

NotFound.description: No such object in this workspace.

Conflict.description: Refused by the object's state machine, a policy, or stale definitions.

Unprocessable.description: The object does not validate against its §3 schema.
